candidateSegments.teachingRole: Speed changes, takeoff, airborne trajectory and landing: visible hook for acceleration and accumulating displacement.

observed.before: Car approaches a ridge on a dirt road.
observed.action: It gains speed, leaves the ridge at~60s, rises/descends while still progressing forward, then lands at~64s.
observed.result: Vertical rise/fall accompanies forward displacement; ground contact changes the motion again.

claimLimits: Not a fitted ideal parabola: ground slopes, camera follows and car pitch changes.
HUD is mph; mass, gravity and physics integration are not exposed.
Do not label impact deceleration as finite constant acceleration over an infinitesimal time.

annotationPlan.target: Hollow wheel-ground separation bracket at takeoff; observed center trail during flight and landing contact outline; no guessed world-speed arrows.
annotationPlan.style: Progressive open contour/short leader/path with labels. No invented game measurements or internal force/skeleton data.
annotationPlan.tracking: These inspected sample frames are planning evidence, not per-frame tracking. Follow actual target; hide at occlusion/out-of-frame; clear at cut.
annotationPlan.captionClearance: Fixed bottom-centre captions and game UI protected; foreground callout should not cover the action.

candidateSegments.teachingRole: Side-view platform jumps make rising, apex and descending readable before our controlled numerical jump model.

observed.before: Mario stands on a brick platform in a two-dimensional section.
observed.action: He jumps up/right onto higher blocks, descends, and jumps again.
observed.result: Each leap has an ascent followed by descent while horizontal movement continues.

claimLimits: 9seconds contains multiple complete jumps; give a short observation sentence rather than stretching it to fit formulas.
End before damage at1480s; head collisions/landings terminate ideal free-flight.
Do not claim actual Mario jump height, acceleration, constant-gravity algorithm or parameter values.

annotationPlan.target: Track feet with small rise/fall arrows; leave actual Dash/Jump prompt readable; no fixed overlaid parabola when camera scrolls.

candidateSegments.sourceSection: 11.6 same height versus same spatial point / jump design
candidateSegments.teachingRole: Sports comparison: forward motion continues during a ski jump, unlike a purely vertical one-dimensional example.

observed.before: Skier descends a snowy slope after an earlier trick.
observed.action: He approaches a mound, takes off around214–215s, rotates and lands around216s, then continues downhill.
observed.result: Landing is farther along the route; returning to a height is not returning to the starting position.

claimLimits: Terrain is sloped, so do not state takeoff and landing heights are exactly equal.
Do not derive projectile physics from trick animation or pretend a calibrated world path.
Visible game speed unit is KMH; no formula value is measured from this source.

annotationPlan.target: Track skier contact point and projected takeoff/landing landmarks; distinguish the translation path from body trick rotation.
